arxiv-1705-01029.title: On-chip quantum interference with heralded photons from two independent micro-ring resonator sources in silicon photonics
arxiv-1705-01029.creator: Imad I. Faruque, Gary F. Sinclair, Damien Bonneau, John G. Rarity, Mark G. Thompson
arxiv-1705-01029.description: Abstract High visibility on-chip quantum interference among indistinguishable single-photons from multiples sources is a key prerequisite for integrated linear optical quantum computing. Resonant enhancement in micro-ring resonators naturally enables brighter, purer and more indistinguishable single-photon production without any tight spectral filtering. The indistinguishability of heralded single-photons from multiple micro-ring resonators has not been measured in any photonic platform.

arxiv-1904-03451.title: Doodle to Search: Practical Zero-Shot Sketch-based Image Retrieval
arxiv-1904-03451.creator: Sounak Dey, Pau Riba, Anjan Dutta, Josep Lladós, Yi-Zhe Song
arxiv-1904-03451.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the problem of zero-shot sketch-based image retrieval (ZS-SBIR), where human sketches are used as queries to conduct retrieval of photos from unseen categories. We importantly advance prior arts by proposing a novel ZS-SBIR scenario that represents a firm step forward in its practical application.

arxiv-2202-03561.title: Normal forms of ω \omega -Hamiltonian vector fields with symmetries Email address: phbaptistelli@uem.br (corresponding author), merhernandes@uem.br Email address: eralcilene.terezio@unila.edu.br
arxiv-2202-03561.creator: Patrícia H. Baptistelli, Maria Elenice R. Hernandes, Eralcilene Moreira Terezio
arxiv-2202-03561.description: Abstract In this paper, we present algebraic tools to obtain normal forms of ω \omega -Hamiltonian vector fields under a semisymplectic action of a Lie group, by taking into account the symmetries and reversing symmetries of the vector field. The normal forms resulting from the process preserve the Hamiltonian condition and the types of symmetries of the original vector field.

arxiv-2307-05747.title: Integrating Curricula with Replays: Its Effects on Continual Learning
arxiv-2307-05747.creator: Tee Ren Jie, Mengmi Zhang
arxiv-2307-05747.description: Abstract Humans engage in learning and reviewing processes with curricula when acquiring new skills or knowledge. This human learning behavior has inspired the integration of curricula with replay methods in continual learning agents. The goal is to emulate the human learning process, thereby improving knowledge retention and facilitating learning transfer.

arxiv-2309-00647.title: Improving Small Footprint Few-shot Keyword Spotting with Supervision on Auxiliary Data
arxiv-2309-00647.creator: Seunghan Yang, Byeonggeun Kim, Kyuhong Shim, Simyung Chang
arxiv-2309-00647.description: Abstract Few-shot keyword spotting (FS-KWS) models usually require large-scale annotated datasets to generalize to unseen target keywords. However, existing KWS datasets are limited in scale and gathering keyword-like labeled data is costly undertaking. To mitigate this issue, we propose a framework that uses easily collectible, unlabeled reading speech data as an auxiliary source.

arxiv-2405-19017.title: Efficient Exploration in Average-Reward Constrained Reinforcement Learning: Achieving Near-Optimal Regret With Posterior Sampling
arxiv-2405-19017.creator: Danil Provodin, Maurits Kaptein, Mykola Pechenizkiy
arxiv-2405-19017.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Danil Provodin, Maurits Kaptein, Mykola Pechenizkiy. We present a new algorithm based on posterior sampling for learning in Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDP) in the infinite-horizon undiscounted setting. The algorithm achieves near-optimal regret bounds while being advantageous empirically compared to the existing algorithms.

arxiv-2602-06070.title: Computationally Efficient Laplacian C L -colME PubID: pubid: 979-8-3315-9817-4/26/$31.00 ©2026 IEEE
arxiv-2602-06070.creator: Nikola Stankovic, Student Member, IEEE
arxiv-2602-06070.description: Abstract Decentralized collaborative mean estimation (colME) is a fundamental task in heterogeneous networks. Its graph-based variants B-colME and C-colME achieve high scalability of the problem. This paper evaluates the consensus-based C-colME framework, which relies on doubly stochastic averaging matrices to ensure convergence to the oracle solution.

pmc-11650180.title: Fractal motor activity during wakefulness and sleep: a window into depression recency and symptom recurrence
pmc-11650180.creator: O. Minaeva, H. Riese, S. H. Booij, F. Lamers, E. J. Giltay, F. A. J. L. Scheer, K. Hu
pmc-11650180.description: BackgroundMotor activity fluctuations in healthy adults exhibit fractal patterns characterized by consistent temporal correlations across wide-ranging time scales. However, these patterns are disrupted by aging and psychiatric conditions. This study aims to investigate how fractal patterns vary across the sleep–wake cycle, differ based on individuals' recency of depression diagnosis, and change before and after a depressive episode.

pmc-12852709.title: Application of porosity logs for cyclostratigraphic analysis in the absence of gamma ray logs
pmc-12852709.creator: Amir Alimardanian, Ali Kodkhodaie, Mohsen Aleali, Mehran Arian, Davood Jahani
pmc-12852709.description: High-resolution cyclostratigraphic and sequence stratigraphic analyses are often compromised and lead to incorrect interpretations due to the unavailability or critical, proven errors in the reference Gamma-Ray (GR) and Density (RHOB) logs in hydrocarbon wells. This issue creates operational risks, delays, and costly re-logging procedures, directly impacting reservoir modeling and development decisions.

pmc-13480145.creator: Mark C. Elliott, Kasimir P. Gregory, Colan E. Hughes, Benjamin D. Ward
pmc-13480145.description: The stabilization of positive and negative charges by alkyl groups (in particular) in organic compounds is often described as polarizability, but it can also be described as hyperconjugation (and related stereoelectronic effects). To a large extent, how one describes charge stabilization depends on the bonding model used.

pmc-13677978.title: FACS-based isolation and recovery of physiologically distinct bacterial subpopulations from infected insect hosts
pmc-13677978.creator: Hasna Toukabri, Christophe Buisson, Yves Le Vern, Alix Sausset, Mickaël Bourge, Leyla Slamti
pmc-13677978.description: Phenotypic heterogeneity is often encountered during infection but remains challenging to investigate in vivo. Here, using the entomopathogenic spore-former Bacillus thuringiensis with the Galleria mellonella insect larva infection model and Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), we present a workflow that enables the isolation of bacterial subpopulations in distinct physiological states, directly from infected hosts, for downstream characterization.
